chapter: Brown's Band in Chicago and New York
title: The district, halfway house, Bucktown and Bruning's
summary: Subbing in the district and at Bucktown dance places, Bruning's Pavilion.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: played everything else. I guess we played the Dauphine, too. Mm-hmm. Well, then, uh, when, uh, 1915 came along, the district was still open down there. Incidentally, did you play in the district at all?
I worked down there. I think I was something for somebody that was sick. I never cared for that
kind of work, Doc. Well, was there one of these places like the Pup or the Cadillac or the Sousie?

Well, uh, that was for Peggy Anstead. Uh-huh. I think that was Iberville and Franklin. Yeah. And, uh, the, the Brunus was playing that. Merritt. Yeah. And Henny. And I was playing piano with them. Mm-hmm. At that time. No, that's been a long time ago. Did you ever play at the halfway house? Uh, for steady, you mean? No. No, I mean even the sub subbing for somebody. Oh, yeah. I played several times out there, but not as a steady job. You see, I didn't care for those long hours. What about Bucktown?

Bucktown, plenty of times. Plenty of times. I wonder if, uh, I'm correct in my memory. The one place they had those dances was up on stilts and they had one door and one pair of steps leading down and there was

fights that started around there all the time. Well, there used to be Bruning's Pavilion. Yeah. The Brunings were the sheriffs out there. Anybody started a fight got beat up and put in jail. They broke the fighting up pretty quickly. That's Bruning, not Brunus. Bruning. No, not Brunus. Bruning. Nah. They had a little tiny old footbridge across the 17th Street Canal at that time.

What about this place near City Park over the Rhine? You ever remember that place there? No. It was a restaurant right across from there. They had a bar and a restaurant there. I didn't play there, no. Did you ever play out at, uh, what do you call that?
